description: Failure-injection experiment: two threads racing conflicting decisions ('complete' vs 'reject') on the same pending task via the real perform_action() endpoint, with an injected delay forcing the interleaving. Asserts the guarded compare-and-swap update closes the race: exactly one commit succeeds, the other receives an explicit 409 conflict.
environment: local disposable PostgreSQL (matches script's documented methodology)
note_on_methodology: An earlier verification pass in this same session ran this experiment against a REMOTE PostgreSQL instance (192.168.1.244) instead of local, and got 3/4 passes -- one clean failure with 2 successful commits. Re-running against a true local, disposable PostgreSQL (as this script's own docstring specifies) gave 8/8 clean passes. The remote-run failure is attributed to network round-trip latency perturbing the injected race-timing window the test depends on, not a code regression -- the guard holds reliably under the documented (local) test conditions.
